extracted.intended_audience: Department of the Navy commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), and other DON public affairs personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Operational public affairs guidance for preparing, reviewing, approving, and disseminating Department of the Navy public information, media releases, and related communications, with specific rules for classification, OPSEC, privacy, legal, and coordination requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh public interest against privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Serious misconduct by lower-level agency employees generally is not considered of sufficient public interest to outweigh the privacy interest of the employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate public interest vs individual privacy before releasing personal information; do not release private information of lower-level employees based solely on curiosity or minor misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diminished privacy expectation for senior officials
rubrics_metrics.description: DON regards flag and general officers, commanding officers, officers-in-charge, and both uniformed and civilian personnel in similar positions as high-level officials with a diminished expectation of privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that public interest and the need to retain public confidence may justify greater disclosure for high-level officials compared with lower-level personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO clearance and access requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All commanders will ensure PAOs have the adequate clearance and access to policy and classified information in order to best serve the government’s interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide PAOs necessary clearances and access to internal policy/classified materials so they can prepare accurate, authorized releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Releasing authority review responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Each activity will review material prepared for public release to ensure it reveals no classified information or sensitive unclassified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While originators and subordinate commands may provide content, the releasing authority retains responsibility to safeguard classified/sensitive information and must review releases accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-authority review for certain categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories of official DOD information meant for release and prepared by or for DOD personnel will be submitted for review and clearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify categories requiring higher-level clearance and follow supplemental guidance for submission to those authorities before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedures to CHINFO/DIRPA/CNO/Marine Corps for review
rubrics_metrics.description: After command and, if necessary, chain of command review, information releases which fall into any of the above categories must be submitted to CHINFO or DIRPA for policy review and/or to CNO (N09N2) or Marine Corps Code INTC for security review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow chain-of-command review then submit to the designated offices for policy/security review per supplemental guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary review option
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources outside of DOD, or DOD personnel acting in a private capacity, may volunteer to have information reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow voluntary review when offered; coordinate with appropriate offices if external sources seek DON review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection and classification of proposed releases
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs submitting or staffing proposed news releases or statements must ensure that the information contained therein is fully coordinated and properly classified until approved for release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper classification markings and coordination prior to release; do not disclose classified material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on release of classified information
rubrics_metrics.description: News media representatives are not usually given access to classified information; in rare circumstances PAOs will gain specific approval from the Joint Force Commander, CHINFO and OASD(PA); media pool briefings may be contingent on withholding publication until authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only release classified material with explicit approvals from designated authorities; require non-disclosure/publication agreements when authorizing limited briefings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions for inadvertent disclosure of classified material
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reporter or photographer has been given wrongful access, the PAO must immediately contact the command Security Manager. DON personnel will not make any statements concerning the classified information; Security Manager notifies CNO (N09N2) who will coordinate further action, which may include asking deletion or doing nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediately report unauthorized disclosures; avoid commenting publicly; follow Security Manager/CNO directives for remediation per SECNAVINST 5510.36.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational security (OPSEC) pre-release review
rubrics_metrics.description: Information must be reviewed and approved at the appropriate level before release. Each DOD member should be aware of OPSEC issues, whether participating in a formal media event or an informal family event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen all communications for OPSEC concerns and obtain required approvals; train personnel to recognize OPSEC risks even in informal contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Releasable information categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The following information is generally releasable: confirmation of ships and aircraft plainly visible to news media; approximate size of friendly forces (exact numbers normally not provided); casualty figures aboard embarked vessel or aircraft (names withheld until next-of-kin notification); results of completed missions; types and general amounts of ordnance expended; number of aerial combat missions flown in the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, release only obvious/plainly visible facts and general descriptors rather than exact details that could harm operations or safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-releasable information categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The following information is generally not releasable: future plans or operations; detailed vulnerabilities or weaknesses; rules of engagement; security measures, force protection or deceptive actions used as part of the operation; intelligence collection activities including methods, targets, and results; information about downed aircraft or ships while SAR planning is in progress (unless plainly in sight); specific types of ordnance expended and methods; location and activities of special operations forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose planning, vulnerabilities, sensitive procedures, intelligence methods, or specific force/ordnance details unless specifically declassified or authorized by higher operational authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect classified aspects of equipment/procedures/operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Classified aspects of equipment, procedures, and operations must be protected from disclosure because of potential jeopardy to future operations, risk to human life, host nation/allied sensitivities, or disclosure of intelligence methods and sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat all classified technical/operational details as non-releasable and consult security and legal authorities before providing technical information to media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit departures/arrivals timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Ship and unit departures and arrivals are generally releasable on or near the date. Commanders must understand that information at the tactical and operational levels is the most perishable in timeliness and decisions about information release must reflect that understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider timeliness and perishable nature of deployment info; coordinate release timing to balance openness and force protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-terrorism/force protection coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: ASD(PA) is the single point of contact for all PA aspects of U.S. military antiterrorist actions; there is no mandatory requirement to release information, and installation commanders are advised to exercise prudent judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with ASD(PA) on antiterrorism-related communications and exercise caution when deciding whether to release information that could affect force protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: POW/EPW information balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: The need to give accurate and timely information regarding POWs or EPWs must be weighed against operational security and personal privacy; Third Geneva Convention requirements for EPWs must be met; DOD will be point of first release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with Geneva Convention requirements and consult supplemental guidance; coordinate releases concerning POWs/EPWs through designated DOD channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical privacy and HIPAA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal privacy rights of those receiving medical care will be observed as a matter of law and courtesy. The HIPAA Privacy Rules prohibit disclosure of PHI without specific authorization by the patient or by an exception in HIPAA regulations. PAOs must discuss medical information release matters with the judge advocate and facility privacy officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before releasing medical information, obtain HIPAA-compliant authorization or identify a regulatory exception; consult judge advocate and privacy officer for each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible medical condition descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Without a HIPAA-compliant authorization or specific HIPAA exception, it is permissible to release a one-word condition description of a medical condition without reference to the patient by name or other identifier. Only medical professionals are authorized to determine the description as: Good, Fair, Serious, Critical, or Undetermined. A patient’s location or room number should not be given without authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit public medical statements to one-word condition categories determined by medical staff and avoid identifying details or precise locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military justice publicity balance
rubrics_metrics.description: In military justice matters, DON activities must balance individual rights, the public interest, and the best interests of the Navy, with emphasis in that order. Unauthorized disclosure of details on matters referred to a court-martial or under investigation may violate rights, hamper government case, unduly influence litigation, or violate DOJ trial publicity guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult staff or command judge advocate and applicable documents before releasing information about judicial matters; avoid disclosures that could prejudice proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations — non-disclosure until certified complete
rubrics_metrics.description: The substance, details or preliminary findings of ongoing investigations will not be publicly disclosed until the investigation is certified complete and proper authority authorizes disclosure; even when complete, not all findings may be releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid implying that all investigation findings will be disclosed; ensure release authority signs off before any investigative details are provided publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations — release authorities and photography
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands requested to provide information from investigations must have chain-of-command clearance (e.g., NCIS, Naval Safety Center, Assistant JAG). Photography of an event may be released even if attached to an investigation but must be approved by CHINFO; asserting an item 'is part of an investigation' is not an exemption. CHINFO is the final release authority for certain imagery and CVN/platform tapes may be immediately releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify appropriate release authority for the investigation type, obtain CHINFO approval for imagery, and do not rely solely on 'under investigation' as a basis to withhold imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect proprietary and limited-rights information
rubrics_metrics.description: DON is responsible for protecting information derived from proprietary data in which DON has 'limited rights' or 'restricted rights.' Such information must be withheld from public release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not release proprietary or limited-rights data without authorization; consult acquisition/contracting and legal offices when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright permissions before use
rubrics_metrics.description: The written permission of the copyright holder must be obtained before copyrighted material may be used, including reproduction by duplication machine and dissemination in that form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure written copyright permission prior to using third-party copyrighted materials in official releases or distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of press clips must include advisory
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs may select, reproduce and distribute press clips and summaries for official review to inform commanders and key officials. Such clips and summaries must be distributed with an advisory warning against any personal use of the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an advisory (sample provided) with distributed press clips that disclaims endorsement and warns against further reproduction for private use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propriety and special circumstances — ethics constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: No public affairs activity is permitted that would conflict with standards of conduct and government ethics. This prohibits activity that would: interfere with official duties; bring discredit on the government, DON, Navy or Marine Corps; place government decision-making outside official channels; be inconsistent with standards of conduct or create the appearance of a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen PA activities for ethics and conduct conflicts; consult supplemental guidance for specific circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional inquiry awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs need to understand the congressional issues that drive media interest and the extent of influence by media publications on government officials and constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor congressional interests and be prepared to respond in coordination with legislative affairs when media attention parallels congressional concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized local response to congressional inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: If a command is in routine contact with a state’s Congressional delegation and the information requested is routine and of negligible national or DON-wide impact, the command may respond without recourse to higher authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use judgment to respond locally to routine congressional requests but forward copies of correspondence to OLA as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional response timeliness and protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional inquiries will be answered in a timely and professional manner: a full reply within 10 working days, or an interim reply within five working days. Commands will reply directly on routine and non-policy matters and send copies of both incoming and outgoing correspondence to the Office of the Chief of Legislative Affairs (OLA). Members of Congress should receive the information before it is released to the media or the public unless instructed otherwise by CHINFO or OLA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the 5/10 working day response standard, copy OLA on correspondence, and provide Members of Congress the information before public release unless directed otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to contact CHINFO or OLA
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult OLA or CHINFO for guidance in handling a congressional request if: the command has no routine contact with the Member/staff; the request is unusual or extraordinary; the request has potential for wider impact beyond the local level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalate atypical or high-impact requests to CHINFO/OLA for coordination and policy guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on political activities and influences
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD members acting in their official capacity may not engage in activities that associate DOD with any partisan political campaign, election, candidate, cause or issue. Commands must avoid any action or appearance that attempts to influence contact with elected officials or attempts to generate support for a particular DON program or issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PA communications do not advocate, appear partisan, or solicit political support; separate official duties from private political activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naval nuclear propulsion — strict need-to-know
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of any information pertaining to naval nuclear propulsion matters is made on a strict need-to-know basis pursuant to agency regulations and federal statutes; ensure nothing prohibited from public dissemination is included and provide proper perspective recognizing public sensitivity to nuclear issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit proposed releases to CHINFO for review and clearance by CNO (N00N) and cognizant officials; keep CHINFO and CNO informed via chain-of-command on any PA matters related to naval nuclear propulsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: CNO concurrence for local nuclear propulsion statements
rubrics_metrics.description: CNO (N00N) must concur in all statements and responses to press inquiries prior to their release if they concern or are related to local naval nuclear propulsion program work at shipyards and support facilities not otherwise requiring clearance by CHINFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain CNO (N00N) concurrence for local nuclear propulsion-related press responses when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuclear weapons — ASD(PA) security review and release authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Information pertaining to nuclear weapons matters must receive security review at the ASD(PA) level before public release. Authority to release information rests with ASD(PA); commands proposing releases will forward the proposal through the chain to N09N. News media representatives will be referred to CHINFO; FOIA requests forwarded to DNS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Route nuclear-weapons related release proposals through correct channels and do not independently release such information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved responses regarding presence of nuclear weapons
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands will respond to inquiries about the presence of nuclear weapons with approved statements: (a) for ships/aircraft/submarines: general policy not to deploy, but do not discuss presence/absence on specific units; (b) for shore stations/strategic submarines/supporting ships/container ships: 'neither confirm nor deny' policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed approved language when asked about nuclear weapons presence; do not provide location-specific confirmations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuclear weapons accidents/incidents — PA responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: In the United States, ASD(PA) retains initial public affairs responsibility for nuclear weapons accidents and incidents; in overseas areas the appropriate Combatant Commander retains responsibility (except for weapon loss/theft/seizure) in coordination with ASD(PA). ASD(PA) and IRF/RTF Commanders are required to confirm presence/absence of nuclear weapons when necessary for public safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate PA response for nuclear incidents with ASD(PA) and IRF/RTF; release information as required to protect public safety and reduce alarm, and follow notification protocols for authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRAC — follow Public Affairs Guidance (PAG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Base Realignments and Closures (BRAC) are contentious; each BRAC process will have specific PAG. All commanders and their PA representatives will become familiar with that PAG and will adhere to it. Supplemental PAG may be issued within DON.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and follow the BRAC-specific PAG when handling BRAC-related communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public affairs planning roles — CHINFO/DIRPA and subordinate commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: CHINFO and DIRPA are responsible for DON strategic communications plans and establishment of overall public affairs strategy, themes and core messages. Commands with a military or civilian PAO will develop detailed public affairs plans for matters over which they have cognizance. Commands without PAOs are not required to have a plan but should have sufficient guidance for short-notice media involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align command-level public affairs plans with CHINFO/DIRPA strategic guidance and maintain localized internal information plans or adopt superior command plans as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanders' public information responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders are ultimately responsible for the public affairs program at their command; they will ensure accurate and continuous flow of timely information with appropriate consideration for security, accuracy, and propriety — 'maximum disclosure, minimum delay.' Commanders should delegate release authority to the command PAO and give PAO direct access to policymakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegate appropriately, provide PAO access to leadership and operations, and support timely, accurate information flow while balancing security and propriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowing journalist access with AT/FP constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the parameters of the command Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection posture, commanders will allow credentialed journalists access to their command (with command escort as feasible) and not interfere with the reporting process. Journalists should be permitted open access to unclassified aspects of military vehicles, locations, personnel, aircraft and vessels, subject to special operations restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate reasonable media access to unclassified areas while enforcing AT/FP measures and special operations restrictions as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders will not use or allow disinformation activities or deception operations intended to misinform, deny releasable information to or mislead the American public, government, or media. This includes misinforming the media about military capabilities and intentions in ways that could influence decision makers and public opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not engage in deceptive PA practices; ensure truthfulness and avoid actions intended to mislead audiences or policymakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO responsibilities — access, accuracy, privacy protection
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs are responsible for guaranteeing open, timely and uninhibited access to public information except where restricted by law, security classification or privacy statutes. They will make reasonable efforts to communicate information to external and internal audiences, protect privacy, act as liaisons (not interfere with reporting except to correct inaccuracies), expedite the flow of information, and ensure accurate coverage by encouraging understanding of facts and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must balance openness with legal/security/privacy constraints, coordinate information, and ensure spokespersons convey consistent, accurate messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO duty to inform chain of items of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs will inform the immediate public affairs chain of command about items with national or international media interest; those with local media interest when expected to reach the attention of flag or general officers; and those involving real, perceived or anticipated security breaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalate significant media-interest items and security-related matters promptly up the PA chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial/privately acting PAOs rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Off-duty PAOs and other DON members acting in a private capacity may prepare information for public release through non-DOD forums if: no laws/regulations are violated; ethical standards are maintained; activities not conducted during duty hours or using DOD resources; and no official DON information is released which is not generally available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure separation between private speech and official duties and avoid using official resources or privileged information when acting privately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination and lowest-appropriate-level release
rubrics_metrics.description: Information release will be coordinated with the appropriate offices, subject-matter experts, and/or activities internal and external to the command. Information will be released at the lowest appropriate level of command unless other guidance dictates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with SMEs and other commands as needed; assess whether the local command can release or whether escalation is required based on impact and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to evaluate before release
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands will evaluate factors such as subject matter, anticipated impact, the scope of expected media coverage (local or national), and, for speeches, the prominence of the speaking venue when deciding release level and coordination needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these factors to determine appropriate coordination, release authority, and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration for accuracy and unified messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: All PAOs with some responsibility on an issue will closely collaborate to ensure accuracy and comprehensiveness, and that all spokespersons have the same information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate inter-office to produce consistent messages and avoid contradictions among spokespersons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding cannot be arbitrary; alternatives to 'no comment'
rubrics_metrics.description: Information cannot be withheld arbitrarily or merely to avoid criticism or embarrassment. 'No comment' is never an appropriate response. Alternatives: 'I have nothing to release on that subject.' or 'An investigation is under way, and it would be inappropriate for me to comment at this time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual responses where possible; avoid stonewalling—use specified alternative phrasings to decline to comment appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications and handling when a death occurs
rubrics_metrics.description: When a DON member dies, the local command may not be the releasing authority of the information. Even when it is, they must adhere to next-of-kin notification guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow next-of-kin notification procedures before releasing names or details; coordinate with higher authorities when local command is not the releasing authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events of intense public interest — prompt candor and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For events such as mishaps, accidents, or emergencies, information will be disseminated fully, candidly and promptly. First release of what happened should be made within one hour of command awareness of an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize immediate, factual release within the one-hour target for high-interest incidents; delay or tardiness can be perceived as concealment and exacerbate public distrust.
